60 Skincare Brands That Send PR to Small Influencers in 2026

If you have a small following and you love skincare, this is the most useful list you will read this year. Skincare is one of the easiest categories to get PR in, because the product is affordable for brands to send and the content converts. Brands genuinely want creators with a few thousand engaged followers, not just the big accounts.

Below are 60 skincare brands that actively send PR to small and micro influencers in 2026, grouped by how you actually get on the list: brands with open application forms, brands that take email pitches, and budget-friendly brands that work with nano creators. Every entry has a realistic follower floor. Treat these as soft guides, because a strong engagement rate beats a big number every single time.

This is the companion to our broader free creator PR list and our K-Beauty PR list. If you want forms specifically, our directory of open PR application forms goes wider across categories.

Why Skincare Is the Easiest PR to Land

Three reasons skincare brands love small creators:

  • Low product cost. A serum costs the brand a few dollars to send. They can afford to seed dozens of micro creators for the price of one macro deal.
  • Skincare content converts. People trust a small creator showing real results far more than a polished celebrity ad. Save rates and "where can I buy this" comments are gold to a brand.
  • Niche audiences are valuable. If your followers are people with acne, rosacea, or a specific skin goal, a brand can target them precisely. That is worth more than a broad audience double your size.

So if you have been holding back because you think 3,000 followers is too few, stop. It is plenty for skincare PR if your content is genuine and your engagement is healthy.

Budget & Nano-Friendly Skincare Brands

If you are just starting out, these brands are the friendliest to creators under 2,000 followers. Product cost is low, so they seed widely and care most about real, engaging content.

  • e.l.f. Skin: Holy Hydration line, very active creator program, works with tiny accounts.
  • CeraVe: derm darling, recruits micro creators for routine and barrier content constantly.
  • The Ordinary: DECIEM works with creators who can explain actives clearly. Education over aesthetics.
  • Cetaphil: gentle cleanser staple, regional programs that take small creators.
  • Nivea: affordable and broad, regional PR seeds creators for body and face.
  • Simple: sensitive skin focus, great for beginner skincare creators.
  • Bubble: built its whole brand on Gen Z micro creators.
  • Byoma: barrier-repair brand that seeds nano creators heavily.
  • Hero Cosmetics: Mighty Patch creators include very small accounts.
  • Starface: playful patches, recruits Gen Z nano creators.
  • Good Molecules: budget actives, generous with PR to small creators.
  • Inkey List: affordable and education-led, friendly to micro creators.
  • Naturium: approachable actives, active creator seeding.
  • Geek & Gorgeous: cult affordable brand, very micro friendly.
  • Beauty of Joseon: K-Beauty hero, works with nano creators doing honest reviews.
  • COSRX: Snail Mucin fame, recruits micro creators in rolling rounds.
  • Anua: Heartleaf Toner, recruits short-form creators constantly.
  • Numbuzin: high response rate for small creators right now.
  • mixsoon: single-ingredient minimalist brand that loves micro creators.
  • Skin1004: Centella ampoule, responsive to small creators.

'I had 1,400 followers and an acne-focused account. I applied to four budget brands from a list like this and three sent PR within a month. Brands wanted my audience because they had the exact skin concern the products treat.'

Sara J., Skincare Creator, 1.4K followers

How to Get Picked With a Small Following

Small creators win PR by being specific and credible, not big. Here is what actually moves the needle:

  • Pick a lane. An account about "acne-prone, oily skin" is far more pitchable than a general lifestyle feed. Brands can match you to a product instantly.
  • Show your engagement rate. 6 percent on 2K followers beats 1 percent on 20K. Put the number front and centre.
  • Have 8 to 10 skincare posts visible. When a brand clicks your profile, it should be obvious you live in this niche.
  • Lead with results. Before and after, texture shots, and honest reviews convert. Save rates tell brands your content is reference-worthy.
  • Bring a media kit. Even a one-pager signals you are serious. Our free media kit template takes 30 minutes.

The Skincare Pitch Template

Use this for any of the email-pitch brands above. Keep it under 150 words.

Subject: [Your Name] x [Brand]: [Product] content idea


Hi [Name or Team],


I'm [Your Name], a skincare creator on [platform] with [X] followers and a [X]% engagement rate. My audience is [age range], [location], focused on [specific skin concern, e.g. sensitive or acne-prone skin].


I've used your [specific product] for [time] and [one genuine observation, e.g. it's the only cleanser that doesn't leave my skin tight].


I'd love to make a [specific format, e.g. 2-week before/after series] featuring it. My media kit is attached.


Thanks for your time,
[Your Name]
[Handles] / [Media kit link]

Follow up once after seven days. That single bump roughly doubles replies. See our follow-up sequence for the wording.

FAQ

How many followers do I need for skincare PR?

Many skincare brands work with creators from around 1,000 followers, and budget and nano-friendly brands go even lower if your content is genuine. Engagement rate, a focused niche, and clear results matter far more than follower count.

Which skincare brands are easiest for beginners?

Budget and affordable brands seed the widest. e.l.f. Skin, CeraVe, The Ordinary, Bubble, Byoma, Good Molecules, Hero Cosmetics, and The INKEY List all work with very small creators because product cost is low and they value real reviews.

What content do skincare brands want from small creators?

Honest, educational, results-led content. Before and after series, routine demonstrations, ingredient explainers, and texture shots perform best. Short-form video is the most requested format, and high save rates signal your content is worth referencing.

Do I have to post in exchange for skincare PR?

It varies. Some brands send no-strings gifting and hope you post, while structured programs ask for one to three pieces of content per package. Affiliate programs usually require content because you earn commission. Always clarify expectations before accepting.
